point_system.notes: The public-land elk permit draw is random with no points, and it's RESIDENTS ONLY. You must hold a Resident Sportsman Hunting License or Lifetime Sportsman's Permit. In 2026 there were 15 online-draw permits (5 either-sex, 10 antlerless) plus 3 on-site festival permits. Private-land elk is a quota hunt with no draw (residents $5 PLE permit, nonresidents $300 NRE). Hunters can also take elk outside the 5-county Core Elk Zone during deer season. AGFC also runs separate WMA deer and other permit draws.

residents_only_notes: PUBLIC-LAND ELK DRAW IS ARKANSAS-RESIDENT ONLY. Nonresidents can hunt only the private-land quota elk season (NR annual hunting license $410 plus NRE elk permit $300) or take elk incidentally outside the Core Elk Zone.

guide_steps: Create or log in to an AGFC licensing account (agfc.com/license).
Buy the Resident Sportsman's License ($25) first. It's required to apply (residents only).
Between May 1 and June 1, apply under 'Special Hunt Permits' for the public-land elk draw ($5, nonrefundable). You must be 6 or older by the hunt start.
There are no parties or points.
The draw happens at the Buffalo River Elk Festival in Jasper (late June), and winners are notified by email and phone. Attend in person to also be eligible for the 3 on-site permits.

There's no leftover draw. For private land in elk country, residents buy the $5 PLE permit and nonresidents the $300 NRE permit, over the counter. Call nightly to check whether the quota has been met.

Unsuccessful nonresident applicants automatically get 1 preference point AND are charged a mandatory, nonrefundable $60.50 point fee. You can buy a point instead of applying ($60.50 plus fees, May 2 to June 7, online only). Points don't accrue in a year you skip, but aren't lost either. They're wiped when you draw a General deer license, and they don't apply to antlerless-only licenses. Groups of up to 15 get the group's assigned preference (check agency site for averaging). No elk, moose or pronghorn seasons.

residents_only_notes: The draw applies to nonresidents only. Residents buy deer licenses over the counter.

guide_steps: Create or log in to the Go Outdoors Iowa account (gooutdoorsiowa.com). Apply online only. Nonresidents born after Jan 1, 1972 need proof of hunter education.

Apply May 2 to June 7 for the nonresident General deer/Antlerless-only combination license. Pick a zone and a season (Bow, Muzzleloader, or Gun 1/2). The license price ($498) plus hunting license and habitat fee is charged up front.
Groups: up to 15 nonresidents, with a group leader number. All members are drawn or rejected together.
If you're not drawn, license fees are refunded to your card, but you're charged the mandatory $60.50 preference point and lose admin and agent fees.
Point only: buy a preference point ($60.50 plus fees) during May 2 to June 7.

Draw status is emailed before the excess sale. Leftover General licenses go on sale July 25 (2026), along with optional antlerless-only licenses. Holiday antlerless licenses go on sale in mid-December if quota allows.

agency: Kansas Department of Wildlife and Parks

point_system.type: preference (nonresident deer; resident firearm either-species deer; resident antelope); bonus (resident elk)
point_system.notes: ALL nonresident deer permits are draw-only and use preference points. A group of up to 5 uses its lowest member's points. Points reset to zero if you don't apply or buy a point within 5 consecutive years. The nonresident mule deer stamp is a separate draw that doesn't use points. ELK is RESIDENT-ONLY (plus qualifying nonresident tenants), with bonus points of 1 extra draw chance each. Points are lost when drawn or after 5 years without activity, and you can't apply and buy a point in the same year. PRONGHORN draw is resident-only.

residents_only_notes: Elk and pronghorn are Kansas residents only (elk also allows qualifying nonresident tenants). Nonresidents can only get deer, through the April preference-point draw.

guide_steps: Create or log in to a GoOutdoorsKS account (gooutdoorskansas.gov) or call 1-833-587-2164.
NONRESIDENTS: buy the nonresident hunting license ($125) BEFORE applying. It's required at application and nonrefundable.

Nonresident deer: apply April 1-24 (2026 window). Choose a unit plus one adjacent unit and a season (archery, muzzleloader, or firearm), and optionally the mule deer stamp. Your card is charged $475 only if drawn ($25 of it is a nonrefundable application fee).
Groups: up to 5 hunters, same unit and weapon. The first applicant creates the group number and others join. The group draws at its lowest point level.
Points only: choose 'Apply for Points only' under Limited Draw Applications during the window ($25 nonresident deer, $10 resident deer, $12.50 elk). Keep activity at least once every 5 years.
Residents: either-species firearm deer and Fort Riley elk are draws in May-June. Most other resident deer permits are over the counter Aug 5 to Dec 31.
Leftovers: whitetail antlerless-only permits are sold over the counter Aug 5 to Dec 31 (up to 10, with unit limits). Elk Unit 3 permits are over the counter for residents.

agency: Kentucky Department of Fish & Wildlife Resources

point_system.notes: Pure random lottery, no preference or bonus points. Residents who apply for the most years without drawing are auto-entered in a resident-only Loyalty Redraw for unclaimed permits. Nonresidents capped at 10% of drawn permits. Drawn hunters are blocked from reapplying for 3 years.

residents_only_notes: Open to nonresidents (max 10% of drawn permits). The Loyalty Redraw for unpurchased permits is resident-only.

guide_steps: Create or log in to your 'My Profile' account at fw.ky.gov. You'll need your date of birth and SSN.
You don't need a hunting license to apply. Only drawn hunters buy the annual hunting license plus the elk permit.

Between Aug 1 and April 30 (midnight ET), click 'Purchase License' and find the elk applications under 'Permits'. You can apply once each for Bull Firearm, Cow Firearm and Either-Sex Archery/Crossbow, but you can only be drawn for one. Youth 15 and under can also apply for the youth-only hunt.
Each application is $10 and nonrefundable. There are no group or party applications for the draw.
A random drawing is held in early May. Check results in My Profile.
If drawn, buy your elk permit and annual hunting license by midnight June 15, or it goes to the resident-only Loyalty Redraw.
After drawing, apply for a hunting unit (up to 5 choices, random assignment) by June 30. Up to 3 drawn hunters can apply for units as a party.

There are no points and no point-only purchase. Unclaimed permits go to the resident Loyalty Redraw, and there's no public leftover sale. An Out-of-Zone elk permit is sold over the counter for counties outside the 16-county elk zone.
Drawn hunters are blocked for 3 years and must complete the post-season survey by the end of February, or they can't apply the next year.

agency: Maine Department of Inland Fisheries & Wildlife

point_system.notes: Moose uses bonus points, earned on a sliding scale per unsuccessful year: years 1-5 earn 1 point, 6-10 earn 2, 11-15 earn 3, 16+ earn 10. Points are lost if you skip 2 consecutive years, receive a permit, or give incorrect ID info. Residents get at least 90% of permits statewide, nonresidents up to 8%, and lodges up to 2%. Nonresidents may buy extra current-year chances. After drawing a permit there's a 3-year waiting period. Residents 65+ with 30+ points are guaranteed a permit. Maine also runs an antlerless-deer permit lottery, which isn't detailed here.

residents_only_notes: Open to nonresidents (separate allocation, up to 8% statewide and 10% per WMD and season combined with lodges).

deadlines.notes: 2026 applications were online only, April 1 to May 18, 2026 at 11:59 p.m. ET.
Bonus-point-only option at the same $15 fee, same window.

guide_steps: Apply online only at the MDIFW moose lottery site. You'll need your MOSES number, or create one.

You don't need a license to apply, but you must be eligible for a Maine big game license. If drawn, you must buy the big game license ($26 resident, $115 nonresident) before paying for the moose permit.

During the window (April 1 to May 18 in 2026), pay $15 and choose WMDs, seasons (September Bull, October Bull, October Antlerless), whether you'll accept antlerless or another WMD, and a sub-permittee plus alternate. Nonresidents can add extra chances.
Not a group application. Your one sub-permittee can hunt with you. Fees are nonrefundable.
For points only, choose the bonus-point-only option ($15). Apply at least every other year to keep your points.
The drawing is in late June (June 20 in 2026), with results online that evening. Pay for the permit by the mid-July deadline ($52 resident, $585 nonresident).
Unclaimed permits aren't sold over the counter. There's also a moose permit auction and permit swap and transfer rules.

point_system.notes: Elk uses a weighted lottery: 1 chance per past unsuccessful year since 2003, plus 1 for the current application, and it's RESIDENTS ONLY. Bear uses preference points (highest points drawn first) and is open to nonresidents, capped at 5% of licenses per hunt. After an any-elk license you're ineligible for life; after an antlerless-only license, for 10 years. Buying a leftover bear license resets bear points to 0.

residents_only_notes: ELK IS MICHIGAN-RESIDENT ONLY. Nonresidents can't apply or build chances. Nonresidents may apply for bear (max 5% of licenses in any hunt number).

deadlines.notes: The 2026 period was May 1 to June 1. The 2027 dates aren't published yet.

guide_steps: Use a license agent, Michigan.gov/DNRLicenses or the DNR Hunt Fish app. You'll need a MI driver's license, a state ID or a DNR Sportcard ($1).
You don't need a base license to apply. If drawn, buy the base license plus the elk receipt or bear license.
Between May 1 and June 1, buy ONE elk application ($5): 'bull only', 'bull or antlerless', or 'chance only'. Elk applicants must be MI residents with hunter ed (or mentored or apprentice).

For bear, buy ONE application ($5) choosing a BMU and hunt period, or 'preference point only'. Party applications are allowed. Check the agency site for the max party size and how party points are calculated. A party with any nonresident counts as nonresident.
Applications are nonrefundable ($5).
Check results in late June (June 22 in 2026). Drawn elk hunters must attend the mandatory elk orientation.
If you're not drawn, you automatically get +1 elk chance or +1 bear point for next year.

Leftover BEAR licenses may go on sale after the draw (buying one resets points to 0). Elk has no leftover sale, but there's an elk/bear hunt transfer program. The Pure Michigan Hunt ($5 each, unlimited, through Dec 31) is a separate lottery that includes an elk license (check agency site for eligibility).

point_system.type: preference (antlerless deer & special deer hunts); random once-in-a-lifetime (elk); bear lottery (point type: check agency site)
point_system.notes: THERE'S NO STATE MOOSE SEASON (regs: 'There is no state moose hunting season'; only tribal seasons). Elk is a RESIDENT-ONLY, once-in-a-lifetime lottery with parties of 2 sharing one tag. 2 licenses are reserved for applicants with 10+ years of application history. Antlerless deer and special hunt drawings use preference points, kept separately by permit type. Points aren't lost by skipping years, are lost when drawn, and a group uses its lowest member's points. Bear permit-area lottery is open to residents and nonresidents, and the no-quota area is over the counter.

residents_only_notes: ELK IS RESIDENT-ONLY. No moose season at all. Bear and deer lotteries are open to nonresidents.

DNR calendar: 09/9/27 antlerless and special hunt lottery deadline. You enter by declaring a lottery area when buying the firearm or muzzleloader license.

guide_steps: Create or log in to a Minnesota DNR Electronic Licensing System (ELS) account (online or the DNR mobile app).

BEAR: apply in April-May with a bear application ($4), choosing a bear permit area. Groups are allowed: the first applicant creates a lottery group number and others join with that number and their last name. Winners must buy the bear license by Aug 1. Leftover and surplus licenses go on sale first come, first served in early August. The no-quota area is over the counter.

ELK (residents only): apply when the window opens (May 2027), choosing a season, zone and license type, individually or as a party of 2 (one shared tag). Winners attend a mandatory orientation and pay $288. It's once in a lifetime.

ANTLERLESS DEER: buy a firearm or muzzleloader deer license and declare a lottery area by the September deadline to be entered automatically. Unsuccessful applicants gain preference. Surplus permits sell first come, first served in October.
Fees are nonrefundable. There's no separate point-only purchase listed, since deer preference builds by applying.
MOOSE: there's no state season. Don't apply.

There are no antlerless elk permits currently.

No parties, no points, and applications are nonrefundable and nontransferable. Resident landowners must be approved before applying to use the landowner allocation.
Check results by July 1. If drawn, buy your elk permit ($50) or bear permit ($25) starting July 1.
There's no leftover sale. Bear hunters must call 800-668-4045 each day to check whether the zone harvest quota has been met.

agency: North Dakota Game and Fish Department

point_system.type: weighted bonus (deer gun, muzzleloader deer, pronghorn); random lottery (elk, moose, bighorn sheep)
point_system.notes: Weighted lottery: if you miss your first choice in the first lottery, you earn a bonus point. Points are doubled in years 2-4 and cubed from year 5 (e.g. year 5 = 4^3+1 = 65 entries). Elk, moose, and bighorn sheep are not weighted. MOOSE, ELK and PRONGHORN are RESIDENT-ONLY. Nonresidents can apply for deer gun (first lottery) and bighorn sheep (max 1 nonresident license). Nonresident deer bow is over the counter. Check the agency site for any once-in-a-lifetime rules on elk, moose and sheep.

residents_only_notes: Moose, elk and pronghorn lotteries are North Dakota residents only. Nonresidents can apply for deer gun and bighorn sheep (only 1 nonresident sheep license).

deadlines.notes: 2026 deadline was Wed March 25, 2026. Regs say the deadline is set by the Director when the application period opens.
2026 deer gun lottery deadline was Wed June 3, 2026.
2026 pronghorn gun/bow lottery deadline was Wed Aug 5, 2026.
Points accrue when you miss your first choice in the first lottery. Check the agency site for a separate point-only option.

bighorn_sheep.notes: includes $100 nonrefundable application fee. Winners pay an additional $500.

guide_steps: Create or log in to the ND Game and Fish online licensing system (gf.nd.gov, Buy and Apply). You need a hunter education certificate (or apprentice license).
Apply for the species lottery online during its window: elk, moose and sheep (deadline about late March), deer gun (early June), pronghorn (early August).

Fees: for deer gun and pronghorn, the license price is paid at application (the nonresident deer gun price includes a $5 nonrefundable application fee). Check the agency site for how unsuccessful applicants get refunds. Elk, moose and sheep require a nonrefundable application fee of $5 resident or $100 nonresident.
Party/group applications: check agency site for each species.
Missing your first choice in the first deer gun or pronghorn lottery earns a bonus point (doubled in years 2-4, cubed from year 5).
After the first lottery, there are second lotteries and then first-come, first-served leftovers for remaining deer and elk licenses (nonresident deer gun drops to $55 after the 2nd lottery).

point_system.type: preference (deer, antelope, landowner elk); bonus (general bull elk, moving to bonus-squared)
point_system.notes: Deer and antelope draws use preference points: highest points drawn first, and all points are lost when awarded. General bull elk uses bonus points (1 extra chance per point, first-choice bull only). NGPC's 2026 guide says the general elk draw 'is moving to a bonus point squared system'. Antlerless elk is a straight lottery from the same application. GENERAL ELK is RESIDENT-ONLY, but nonresident landowners can apply for landowner elk (0.9 points per year). The bighorn sheep lottery is resident-only and once in a lifetime. Nonresident antelope is limited to archery draw (250), landowner, and late doe/fawn. Party hunting isn't allowed, and you get one elk application per year.

residents_only_notes: General elk draw and the bighorn sheep lottery are resident-only. Nonresident landowners can apply for landowner elk. Nonresidents can draw deer in many units and Statewide Archery/Muzzleloader, but only Statewide Archery for antelope.

No party or group hunting or applications (NGPC: 'Party hunting is not allowed').
Instead of applying, you can buy one preference point (deer or antelope) or one bonus point (resident elk) during the same window.

agency: New Hampshire Fish and Game Department

point_system.notes: Bonus points give 1 extra chance per consecutive year applied without being drawn. You can apply for a point only. Points are lost if you miss a year or accept a permit. One application per person per year. About 85% of permits go to residents, and the nonresident cap is based on the prior year's nonresident hunting license sales. Only 33 permits in 2026 (odds 1 in 109 resident, 1 in 495 nonresident).

residents_only_notes: Open to nonresidents (capped, about 15% of permits).

No group applications, but winners may hunt with a subpermittee and guide.
If you can't hunt this year, submit a bonus-point-only application to keep your streak. Missing a year wipes your points.
There's a random computerized drawing in mid-June, and winners are notified by mail. Pay the permit fee ($150 resident, $500 nonresident). Alternates are drawn too.
There's no leftover sale. The season is 9 days starting the third Saturday in October.

point_system.notes: This isn't a true preference system. Each point is one extra application in a random draw. 1 point per unsuccessful category. New option: buy 1 extra point per category ($10 resident, $50 nonresident). Open to nonresidents.

guide_steps: Create or log in to GoOutdoorsOklahoma.com.

Groups: elk is individual (2 hunters max for walk-in hunts), antelope is individual only, deer allows up to 4. Group points are averaged. Make sure only ONE person submits the group application.

guide_steps: Create a HuntFishPA account (huntfish.pa.gov).
Buy a PA general hunting license first. Since 2026 it's required to apply or buy a point, even for nonresidents (NR adult $101.97).

During the application window (May 1 to July 12 in 2026), buy ONE elk application ($11.97). Add up to 5 choices of season (archery, 1st/2nd/3rd regular), elk hunt zone and antlered or antlerless. Use all 5, since there's no fallback.
You can't apply as a group or party, and you get one application per hunter per year.

If you only want a point, buy the 'Elk Bonus Point Only' ($11.97) instead. You won't be entered in that year's drawing.

agency: South Dakota Game, Fish and Parks

species: Deer (East River, West River, Black Hills, Refuge, Muzzleloader, Custer SP)
point_system.notes: Preference points: 1 per year when unsuccessful for that season. Elk, mountain goat and bighorn get points automatically when you apply and miss. Deer and antelope points must be bought, either by opting in on the application or online from Sept 15 to Dec 15 ($5 resident, $20 nonresident). Points reset when drawn using points. Elk drawn with points means losing them and waiting 9 years for that season. Groups use the lowest member's points. ELK, bighorn and goat are effectively RESIDENT-ONLY (elk fee schedule lists resident prices only). Many deer seasons (Custer SP, East River, Special Buck, Muzzleloader) are resident-only. West River deer and Prairie antelope are open to nonresidents with a small allocation.

residents_only_notes: Elk, bighorn and mountain goat are resident-only. East River deer, the Special Buck seasons, Muzzleloader and Custer State Park deer are resident-only. Nonresidents can apply for West River deer, Black Hills deer (check agency site) and Prairie firearms or Special antelope.

guide_steps: Create or log in to your GFP account at gfp.sd.gov. All draw applications are online only, and you'll need the last 4 digits of your SSN.
You don't need a base license to apply. Your card is charged only if you draw or opt into a preference point. Anyone 18+ also needs a Habitat Stamp ($10 resident, $25 nonresident).
Pick the season (Elk, West River deer, East River deer, Black Hills, Prairie antelope, etc.) and up to the allowed choices. Residents can apply for 2 of the 6 firearm deer seasons in the first draw.
Groups: up to 6 people (only 2 for elk, none for bighorn or goat). The group uses the lowest point balance. Residents and nonresidents can group where both are allowed.

Elk, bighorn and goat applications cost $10 (nonrefundable) and earn a point automatically if you miss. For deer and antelope, tick the preference-point option ($5 resident, $20 nonresident) or buy a point online Sept 15 to Dec 15.
Results come about 1-2 weeks after each deadline. There are 2-4 sequential draws, so unsuccessful or unused tags roll into the next draw.

Leftover licenses sell first come, first served after the final draw (deer leftovers from Sept 9 in 2026). Returned licenses cost $10 resident or $30 nonresident to return by Aug 1, and make you ineligible for later draws that season.

Drawn applicants can't reapply for 10 years. The youth elk hunt is resident-only. Separate WMA Big Game quota hunts use priority points: 1 per unsuccessful year, sorted highest-first, reset to 0 when drawn, and averaged within a party.

residents_only_notes: Nonresidents can apply for the regular elk quota hunt (max 25% of winners). The Young Sportsman elk permit is resident youth only (ages 13-16).

guide_steps: Create a GoOutdoorsTennessee.com account (or use the TWRA On The Go app, a license agent, or a regional office). You can't apply by mail.

No parties are allowed for elk. You can edit your application until the deadline.
Drawing is random (no points). Check results in your account after the drawing. Winners can't reapply for 10 years.

There's no elk point-only option and no elk leftover sale. For WMA deer and bear quota hunts (June 9-July 21, 2027), you can apply as a party or buy point-only (individual). Unsuccessful applicants gain 1 priority point, and leftover permits don't affect points.

point_system.notes: Loyalty Points were formerly called Preference Points. You earn 1 point per category per season when you apply. Points apply to every application in that category, are CUBED in the drawing, and reset to zero when you're drawn. Group points are averaged (round half up). USFS and E-Postcard hunts earn no points.

residents_only_notes: Drawn hunts are generally open to residents and nonresidents. Check each hunt's eligibility in the catalog. Nonresidents must hold the Non-resident General Hunting License ($315) to hunt deer, pronghorn or bighorn.

guide_steps: Create an account in the Texas Public Hunt System (tpwd.texas.gov drawn hunts, 'Create Account').
Pick hunts from the 2026-27 Drawn Hunt Catalog. Each category has its own deadline (pronghorn Aug 15, gun deer Sep 15, gun mule deer Oct 1, exotic Oct 15, guided bighorn Nov 1 in 2026).
Apply individually or as a group. Group Loyalty Points are averaged. Pay $3 per adult per application ($10 for Private Lands or Guided). It's nonrefundable.
Every application earns 1 Loyalty Point in that category. There's no separate point-only purchase.

If drawn, buy the permit by the permit deadline: $80 standard, $130 extended. You also need a Texas hunting license ($25 resident, $315 nonresident general) and any required endorsements. If the initial winners don't buy, there's a secondary permit deadline.
Other options: the Annual Public Hunting Permit (separate) covers USFS and E-Postcard hunts, which have no application fee and earn no points.

guide_steps: Create or log in to Go Outdoors Virginia (gooutdoorsvirginia.com), or call DWR customer service to apply by phone.

Apply during the window (Feb 1 to Mar 31 in 2026). The application fee is nonrefundable.
There are no groups or parties and no points. Each applicant gets a random number, and licenses are offered in number order (1 zone-resident slot, max 1 nonresident).

guide_steps: Create or log in to a Go Wild account (gowild.wi.gov) or visit a license agent.
You don't need a license to apply. Winners buy the license after the draw.
ELK (residents only): between March 1 and May 31, buy a Bull Elk Application and/or an Antlerless Elk Application ($10 each), and pick a unit or unit group with a quota.
There are no groups or points for elk. Applications are nonrefundable.

Elk winners are notified in early June, must take the mandatory DNR elk hunter education course, then buy the $49 elk license. It's a once-in-a-lifetime license, and transferring it makes both people ineligible for the future.
BEAR: by Dec 10, apply on Go Wild ($4.50), choosing a zone or the preference-point-only option. If you're not drawn, you gain 1 point.
Bear drawing results come out in early February. Winners buy the Class A bear license ($49 resident, $251 nonresident).
There's no leftover sale for elk. Bear and elk awards can be transferred under the DNR permit-transfer rules.
